ko.title: 다른 중앙은행들은 대기하는 동안 금리를 인상하는 이유: 영은회와 호주중앙은행이 다시 금리를 인상하는 이유

segments.src: For much of the past two years, the global story in monetary policy was about cutting.
segments.tr: 지난 2년 동안 대부분의 기간 동안 통화 정책의 세계적인 화두는 금리 인하였다.

segments.src: Now a few central banks are moving the other way.
segments.tr: 이제 일부 중앙은행들은 반대 방향으로 움직이고 있다.

segments.src: The Bank of England has raised its benchmark rate to 4%, its first increase in more than three years.
segments.tr: 영국 중앙은행(Bank of England)은 기준금리를 4%로 인상했으며, 이는 3년 이상 만에 처음 있는 인상이다.

segments.src: The Reserve Bank of Australia has tightened five times this year.
segments.tr: 호주중앙은행(Reserve Bank of Australia)은 올해 다섯 차례 긴축을 단행했다.

segments.src: This article explains what is behind those decisions and what they could mean for U.S.
segments.tr: 이 기사는 이러한 결정의 배경과 미국 독자들에게

segments.src: readers.
segments.tr: 어떤 의미를 가질 수 있는지 설명한다.

segments.src: *This is general information and not investment or financial advice.
segments.tr: *본 내용은 일반적인 정보 제공을 위한 것이며 투자나 재정 자문이 아닙니다.

segments.src: Details of policy decisions can change quickly, so check official central bank statements for the latest figures.*
segments.tr: 정책 결정 세부 사항은 빠르게 바뀔 수 있으므로 최신 수치는 공식 중앙은행 성명을 확인하시기 바랍니다.*

segments.src: ## What happened
segments.tr: ## 무슨 일이 일어났는가

segments.src: - **United Kingdom:** The Bank of England lifted its policy rate to 4%. That is the first rate rise in over three years, and it ends a period in which markets had mostly expected cuts.
segments.tr: - **영국:** 영국 중앙은행은 정책금리를 4%로 인상했다. 이는 3년 넘게 만에 처음 있는 금리 인상이며, 시장이 대부분 금리 인하를 예상했던 시기에 마침표를 찍는 것이다.

segments.src: - **Australia:** The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates five times this year. That makes it one of the most active tightening central banks among advanced economies.
segments.tr: - **호주:** 호주중앙은행은 올해 다섯 차례 금리를 인상했다. 이로 인해 호주는 선진국 중 가장 적극적으로 긴축을 단행하는 중앙은행 중 하나가 되었다.

segments.src: Both banks have said their decisions follow the data.
segments.tr: 두 은행 모두 자신들의 결정이 데이터에 따른 것이라고 밝혔다.

segments.src: Neither has described them as a break from their inflation targets.
segments.tr: 어느 은행도 이를 인플레이션 목표치에서의 이탈로 규정하지 않았다.

segments.src: Each says it is trying to bring inflation back toward its goal.
segments.tr: 각각 인플레이션을 다시 목표치로 되돌리기 위해 노력하고 있다고 말한다.

segments.src: ## Why inflation is picking up again
segments.tr: ## 인플레이션이 다시 고개를 드는 이유

segments.src: Inflation rarely rises for one reason.
segments.tr: 인플레이션이 한 가지 이유로만 상승하는 경우는 드물다.

segments.src: Several forces are commonly cited in cases like these:
segments.tr: 이러한 경우 흔히 다음과 같은 여러 요인이 언급된다:

segments.src: 1. **Sticky services prices.** Wages, rents and insurance costs tend to move slowly. When they keep rising, headline inflation is slow to cool.
segments.tr: 1. **끈질긴 서비스 가격.** 임금, 임대료, 보험료는 천천히 움직이는 경향이 있다. 이 비용들이 계속 상승하면 헤드라인 인플레이션은 둔화되는 속도가 느려진다.

segments.src: 2. **Energy and food costs.** Swings in energy and food prices can lift inflation quickly. They also affect what households expect inflation to be.
segments.tr: 2. **에너지 및 식품 비용.** 에너지와 식품 가격의 변동은 인플레이션을 빠르게 끌어올릴 수 있다. 또한 가계가 예상하는 인플레이션 수준에도 영향을 미친다.

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** Where employers still struggle to hire, wage growth can stay high enough to keep price pressure up.
segments.tr: 3. **타이트한 노동 시장.** 고용주들이 여전히 채용에 어려움을 겪는 곳에서는 임금 상승률이 가격 압력을 유지할 만큼 높게 유지될 수 있다.

segments.src: 4. **Inflation expectations.** If households and firms expect higher prices, they may set wages and prices accordingly. Central banks want to stop that cycle early.
segments.tr: 4. **인플레이션 기대치.** 가계와 기업이 더 높은 가격을 예상하면 그에 맞춰 임금과 가격을 설정할 수 있다. 중앙은행들은 그 악순환을 조기에 차단하고자 한다.

segments.src: 5. **Currency moves.** A weaker local currency makes imports more expensive, which can feed into consumer prices.
segments.tr: 5. **환율 움직임.** 현지 통화 약세는 수입품 가격을 더 비싸게 만들며, 이는 소비자 물가에 반영될 수 있다.

segments.src: Which of these matters most differs by country.
segments.tr: 이 중 어떤 요인이 가장 중요한지는 국가별로 다르다.

segments.src: That is one reason central banks do not all move at the same time.
segments.tr: 이것이 바로 중앙은행들이 모두 동시에 움직이지 않는 이유 중 하나이다.

segments.src: ## Why some banks hike while others wait
segments.tr: ## 일부 은행이 금리를 인상하는 동안 다른 은행이 대기하는 이유

segments.src: Central banks answer to different data.
segments.tr: 중앙은행들은 각기 다른 데이터에 대응한다.

segments.src: A bank that sees inflation staying above target, or rising again, may judge that waiting is riskier than acting.
segments.tr: 인플레이션이 목표치 위에 머물거나 다시 상승하는 것을 보는 은행은 대기하는 것이 행동하는 것보다 더 위험하다고 판단할 수 있다.

segments.src: A bank that sees slowing growth and cooling prices may choose to hold.
segments.tr: 성장 둔화와 물가 안정세를 보는 은행은 금리를 동결하기로 선택할 수 있다.

segments.src: Rate increases also carry costs.
segments.tr: 금리 인상에는 비용도 따른다.

segments.src: Higher borrowing costs weigh on mortgage holders, small businesses and government budgets.
segments.tr: 높아진 차입 비용은 모기지 대출자, 소상공인, 정부 예산에 부담을 준다.

segments.src: Policymakers weigh those costs against the risk of letting inflation settle at a higher level.
segments.tr: 정책 입안자들은 이러한 비용과 인플레이션이 더 높은 수준에서 고착화되도록 방치할 위험을 저울질한다.

segments.src: ## What it could mean for the dollar
segments.tr: ## 달러화에 미칠 수 있는 의미

segments.src: Exchange rates reflect the gap between interest rates in different places.
segments.tr: 환율은 지역별 금리 격차를 반영한다.

segments.src: When other central banks raise rates while the Federal Reserve holds steady, the difference narrows.
segments.tr: 연방준비제도(Fed)가 금리를 동결하는 동안 다른 중앙은행들이 금리를 인상하면 그 격차가 좁혀진다.

segments.src: That can make other currencies somewhat more attractive relative to the dollar.
segments.tr: 이는 다른 통화들이 달러에 비해 다소 더 매력적으로 보이게 만들 수 있다.

segments.src: Several points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: 몇 가지 점을 염두에 둘 가치가 있다:

segments.src: - Currency moves depend on many factors, not just rate differences. These include growth, trade flows, and investor appetite for risk.
segments.tr: - 환율 움직임은 금리 차이뿐만 아니라 성장, 무역 흐름, 위험에 대한 투자자 선호 등 많은 요인에 좌우된다.

segments.src: - The dollar often strengthens during periods of global uncertainty, which can offset the effect of narrower rate gaps.
segments.tr: - 달러화는 종종 글로벌 불확실성 시기에 강세를 보이며, 이는 금리 격차 축소의 효과를 상쇄할 수 있다.

segments.src: - Markets usually price in expected moves before they happen. A rate rise that was widely expected may have little effect on the day.
segments.tr: - 시장은 대개 예상되는 움직임을 사전에 가격에 반영한다. 널리 예상되었던 금리 인상은 당일에 거의 영향을 미치지 않을 수 있다.

segments.src: ## Import prices and everyday costs
segments.tr: ## 수입 물가와 일상 비용

segments.src: A softer dollar makes imported goods more expensive for U.S.
segments.tr: 달러화 약세는 미국

segments.src: buyers.
segments.tr: 바이어들에게 수입품 가격을 더 비싸게 만든다.

segments.src: That can show up in:
segments.tr: 이는 다음에서 나타날 수 있다:

segments.src: - Electronics, vehicles and parts, and other manufactured goods
segments.tr: - 전자기기, 차량 및 부품, 기타 제조업 제품

segments.src: - Some foods and beverages that are brought in from abroad
segments.tr: - 해외에서 들여오는 일부 식품 및 음료

segments.src: - Raw materials that U.S. manufacturers buy overseas
segments.tr: - 미국 제조업체들이 해외에서 구매하는 원자재

segments.src: The effect is usually gradual.
segments.tr: 그 영향은 대개 점진적이다.

segments.src: Retailers often hold prices for a while, and many firms hedge currency risk.
segments.tr: 소매업체들은 종종 한동안 가격을 유지하며, 많은 기업들이 환율 위험을 헤지한다.

segments.src: Any pass-through to consumer prices also depends on competition and demand.
segments.tr: 소비자 물가로의 전가 여부 역시 경쟁과 수요에 따라 달라진다.

segments.src: ## What it could mean for the Fed
segments.tr: ## 연준에 미칠 수 있는 의미

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets policy based on U.S.
segments.tr: 연방준비제도는 미국

segments.src: conditions.
segments.tr: 상황에 기반하여 정책을 수립한다.

segments.src: Foreign rate moves are not a direct input to its decisions.
segments.tr: 외국의 금리 인상은 연준 결정의 직접적인 투입 요소가 아니다.

segments.src: They can still matter in indirect ways:
segments.tr: 그럼에도 불구하고 간접적인 방식으로 중요할 수 있다:

segments.src: - **Inflation signals.** If global price pressures are rising, it may be a warning for U.S. import prices and inflation expectations.
segments.tr: - **인플레이션 신호.** 글로벌 물가 압력이 상승하고 있다면, 이는 미국의 수입 물가와 인플레이션 기대치에 대한 경고음일 수 있다.

segments.src: - **Financial conditions.** A weaker dollar loosens financial conditions a little. That could be a factor if the Fed wants to keep policy tight enough to bring inflation down.
segments.tr: - **금융 여건.** 달러화 약세는 금융 여건을 약간 완화시킨다. 이는 연준이 인플레이션을 낮추기 위해 충분히 긴축적인 정책 기조를 유지하고자 할 때 변수가 될 수 있다.

segments.src: - **Market expectations.** Investors often compare central banks. Moves abroad can change how markets price the path of U.S. rates.
segments.tr: - **시장 기대치.** 투자자들은 종종 중앙은행들을 서로 비교한다. 해외의 움직임은 시장이 미국 금리의 경로를 가격에 반영하는 방식을 바꿀 수 있다.

segments.src: None of this means the Fed will follow.
segments.tr: 그렇다고 해서 연준이 이를 따라갈 것이라는 의미는 아니다.

segments.src: Officials have stressed that they will respond to U.S.
segments.tr: 관계자들은 미국의

segments.src: inflation, employment and growth data.
segments.tr: 인플레이션, 고용, 성장 데이터에 대응할 것임을 거듭 강조해왔다.

segments.src: What to watch is whether the U.S.
segments.tr: 지켜봐야 할 점은 미국의

segments.src: data begin to look like those abroad.
segments.tr: 데이터가 해외 데이터와 닮아가기 시작하는지 여부이다.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## 다음으로 주목할 점

segments.src: - **U.S. inflation reports,** especially services prices and import prices
segments.tr: - **미국의 인플레이션 지표,** 특히 서비스 가격과 수입 물가

segments.src: - **Fed communications,** including meeting statements, minutes and speeches
segments.tr: - **연준의 소통,** 회의 성명, 의사록 및 연설 포함

segments.src: - **Next decisions from the Bank of England and the Reserve Bank of Australia,** and whether they signal more increases or a pause
segments.tr: - **영국 중앙은행과 호주중앙은행의 다음 결정,** 그리고 추가 인상 신호를 보내는지 아니면 일시 중지를 시사하는지 여부

segments.src: - **The dollar's exchange rate** against the pound and the Australian dollar
segments.tr: - **파운드화와 호주달러 대비 달러화의 환율**

segments.src: - **Energy and food prices,** which can change the inflation picture quickly
segments.tr: - **인플레이션 국면을 빠르게 바꿀 수 있는 에너지 및 식품 가격**

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 결론

segments.src: The Bank of England's move to 4% and Australia's run of five increases show that the fight against inflation is not over everywhere.
segments.tr: 영국 중앙은행의 4% 금리 인상과 호주의 다섯 차례 연속 인상은 인플레이션과의 싸움이 모든 곳에서 끝나지 않았음을 보여준다.

segments.src: For the United States, the most likely effects are indirect: some pressure on the dollar, possibly higher import costs over time, and more attention on whether U.S.
segments.tr: 미국의 경우 가장 유력한 영향은 간접적이다. 달러화에 대한 일부 압력, 시간에 따른 수입 비용 상승 가능성, 그리고 미국의

segments.src: inflation follows the same path.
segments.tr: 인플레이션이 같은 경로를 따르는지에 대한 더 많은 관심이다.

segments.src: How much this matters will depend on the data in the coming months.
segments.tr: 이것이 얼마나 중요할지는 향후 몇 달간의 데이터에 달려 있을 것이다.

segments.src: ## What happened
segments.tr: ## 发生了什么

segments.src: - **United Kingdom:** The Bank of England lifted its policy rate to 4%. That is the first rate rise in over three years, and it ends a period in which markets had mostly expected cuts.
segments.tr: - **英国：**英国央行将政策利率上调至 4%。这是三年多来的首次加息，打破了市场此前普遍预期降息的时期。

segments.src: - **Australia:** The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates five times this year. That makes it one of the most active tightening central banks among advanced economies.
segments.tr: - **澳大利亚：**澳大利亚储备银行今年已加息五次。这使其成为发达经济体中最活跃的收紧政策的央行之一。

segments.src: Both banks have said their decisions follow the data.
segments.tr: 两家央行都表示，其决策是根据数据做出的。

segments.src: Neither has described them as a break from their inflation targets.
segments.tr: 没有哪家央行将此描述为背离其通胀目标。

segments.src: Each says it is trying to bring inflation back toward its goal.
segments.tr: 双方都表示正在努力将通胀率拉回其目标水平。

segments.src: ## Why inflation is picking up again
segments.tr: ## 为什么通胀再次抬头

segments.src: Inflation rarely rises for one reason.
segments.tr: 通胀很少是因为单一原因而上升的。

segments.src: Several forces are commonly cited in cases like these:
segments.tr: 在类似情况下，通常会引用以下几种力量：

segments.src: 1. **Sticky services prices.** Wages, rents and insurance costs tend to move slowly. When they keep rising, headline inflation is slow to cool.
segments.tr: 1. **具有粘性的服务价格。** 工资、租金和保险成本往往变动缓慢。当它们持续上涨时，整体通胀降温速度就会很慢。

segments.src: 2. **Energy and food costs.** Swings in energy and food prices can lift inflation quickly. They also affect what households expect inflation to be.
segments.tr: 2. **能源和食品成本。** 能源和食品价格的波动会迅速推高通胀。它们也会影响家庭对未来通胀的预期。

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** Where employers still struggle to hire, wage growth can stay high enough to keep price pressure up.
segments.tr: 3. **劳动力市场紧张。** 在雇主仍然难以招聘的地方，工资增长可能会保持在高位，从而持续给价格带来压力。

segments.src: 4. **Inflation expectations.** If households and firms expect higher prices, they may set wages and prices accordingly. Central banks want to stop that cycle early.

segments.src: ## What happened

segments.src: - **United Kingdom:** The Bank of England lifted its policy rate to 4%. That is the first rate rise in over three years, and it ends a period in which markets had mostly expected cuts.
segments.tr: - **Reino Unido:** El Banco de Inglaterra elevó su tipo de interés oficial al 4%. Es la primera subida de tipos en más de tres años y pone fin a un período en el que los mercados esperaban principalmente recortes.

segments.src: - **Australia:** The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates five times this year. That makes it one of the most active tightening central banks among advanced economies.

segments.src: ## Why inflation is picking up again
segments.tr: ## Por qué la inflación vuelve a repuntar

segments.src: Inflation rarely rises for one reason.
segments.tr: La inflación rara vez sube por una sola razón.

segments.src: Several forces are commonly cited in cases like these:
segments.tr: Se suelen citar varias fuerzas en casos como estos:

segments.src: 1. **Sticky services prices.** Wages, rents and insurance costs tend to move slowly. When they keep rising, headline inflation is slow to cool.
segments.tr: 1. **Precios de servicios rígidos.** Los salarios, los alquileres y los costos de seguros tienden a moverse lentamente. Cuando siguen subiendo, la inflación general tarda en enfriarse.

segments.src: 2. **Energy and food costs.** Swings in energy and food prices can lift inflation quickly. They also affect what households expect inflation to be.
segments.tr: 2. **Costes de energía y alimentos.** Las oscilaciones en los precios de la energía y los alimentos pueden elevar la inflación rápidamente. También afectan a lo que los hogares esperan que sea la inflación.

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** Where employers still struggle to hire, wage growth can stay high enough to keep price pressure up.
segments.tr: 3. **Mercados laborales tensos.** Donde los empleadores aún luchan por contratar, el crecimiento salarial puede mantenerse lo suficientemente alto como para mantener la presión sobre los precios.

segments.src: 4. **Inflation expectations.** If households and firms expect higher prices, they may set wages and prices accordingly. Central banks want to stop that cycle early.
segments.tr: 4. **Expectativas de inflación.** Si los hogares y las empresas esperan precios más altos, pueden fijar los salarios y los precios en consecuencia. Los bancos centrales quieren detener ese ciclo a tiempo.

segments.src: 5. **Currency moves.** A weaker local currency makes imports more expensive, which can feed into consumer prices.
segments.tr: 5. **Movimientos de divisas.** Una moneda local más débil encarece las importaciones, lo que puede alimentar los precios al consumidor.

segments.src: ## Why inflation is picking up again

segments.src: 1. **Sticky services prices.** Wages, rents and insurance costs tend to move slowly. When they keep rising, headline inflation is slow to cool.

segments.src: 2. **Energy and food costs.** Swings in energy and food prices can lift inflation quickly. They also affect what households expect inflation to be.
segments.tr: 2. **تكاليف الطاقة والغذاء.** يمكن تقلبات أسعار الطاقة والغذاء أن ترفع التضخم بسرعة. كما أنها تؤثر على ما تتوقع الأسر أن يكون عليه التضخم.

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** Where employers still struggle to hire, wage growth can stay high enough to keep price pressure up.
segments.tr: 3. **أسواق العمل الضيقة.** في الأماكن التي لا يزال أصحاب العمل يعانون فيها من أجل التوظيف، يمكن أن يظل نمو الأجور مرتفعاً بما يكفي للحفاظ على الضغط على الأسعار.

segments.src: 4. **Inflation expectations.** If households and firms expect higher prices, they may set wages and prices accordingly. Central banks want to stop that cycle early.

segments.src: 5. **Currency moves.** A weaker local currency makes imports more expensive, which can feed into consumer prices.

segments.src: For much of the past two years, the global story in monetary policy was about cutting.
segments.tr: Pendant une grande partie des deux dernières années, l'histoire mondiale de la politique monétaire tournait autour des baisses.

segments.src: Now a few central banks are moving the other way.

segments.src: ## What happened
segments.tr: ## Ce qui s'est passé

segments.src: - **United Kingdom:** The Bank of England lifted its policy rate to 4%. That is the first rate rise in over three years, and it ends a period in which markets had mostly expected cuts.
segments.tr: - **Royaume-Uni :** La Banque d'Angleterre a relevé son taux directeur à 4 %. Il s'agit de la première hausse de taux depuis plus de trois ans, et cela met fin à une période où les marchés s'attendaient principalement à des baisses.

segments.src: - **Australia:** The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates five times this year. That makes it one of the most active tightening central banks among advanced economies.
segments.tr: - **Australie :** La Reserve Bank of Australia a relevé ses taux cinq fois cette année. Cela en fait l'une des banques centrales de resserrement les plus actives parmi les économies avancées.

segments.src: Both banks have said their decisions follow the data.
segments.tr: Les deux banques ont déclaré que leurs décisions suivaient les données.

segments.tr: Aucune d'elles n'a qualifié ces mesures de rupture avec leurs objectifs d'inflation.

segments.tr: Chacune affirme chercher à ramener l'inflation vers son objectif.

segments.src: ## Why inflation is picking up again
segments.tr: ## Pourquoi l'inflation repart à la hausse

segments.src: Inflation rarely rises for one reason.
segments.tr: L'inflation augmente rarement pour une seule raison.

segments.src: Several forces are commonly cited in cases like these:
segments.tr: Plusieurs forces sont communément citées dans ce genre de situation :

segments.src: 1. **Sticky services prices.** Wages, rents and insurance costs tend to move slowly. When they keep rising, headline inflation is slow to cool.
segments.tr: 1. **Prix des services rigides.** Les salaires, les loyers et les coûts d'assurance ont tendance à évoluer lentement. Lorsqu'ils continuent d'augmenter, l'inflation globale met du temps à se tasser.

segments.src: 2. **Energy and food costs.** Swings in energy and food prices can lift inflation quickly. They also affect what households expect inflation to be.
segments.tr: 2. **Coûts de l'énergie et de l'alimentation.** Les fluctuations des prix de l'énergie et de l'alimentation peuvent faire monter rapidement l'inflation. Elles influencent également les anticipations d'inflation des ménages.

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** Where employers still struggle to hire, wage growth can stay high enough to keep price pressure up.
segments.tr: 3. **Marchés du travail tendus.** Là où les employeurs ont toujours du mal à embaucher, la croissance des salaires peut rester suffisamment élevée pour maintenir la pression sur les prix.

segments.src: 4. **Inflation expectations.** If households and firms expect higher prices, they may set wages and prices accordingly. Central banks want to stop that cycle early.
segments.tr: 4. **Anticipations d'inflation.** Si les ménages et les entreprises s'attendent à des prix plus élevés, ils peuvent fixer les salaires et les prix en conséquence. Les banques centrales veulent endiguer ce cycle dès le début.

segments.src: 5. **Currency moves.** A weaker local currency makes imports more expensive, which can feed into consumer prices.
segments.tr: 5. **Mouvements des devises.** Une monnaie locale plus faible renchérit les importations, ce qui peut se répercuter sur les prix à la consommation.

segments.src: Which of these matters most differs by country.
segments.tr: L'importance de ces facteurs varie selon les pays.

segments.src: That is one reason central banks do not all move at the same time.
segments.tr: C'est l'une des raisons pour lesquelles les banques centrales n'agissent pas toutes en même temps.

segments.src: ## What it could mean for the dollar

segments.src: That can make other currencies somewhat more attractive relative to the dollar.
segments.tr: Cela peut rendre d'autres devises un peu plus attractives par rapport au dollar.

segments.src: Several points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: Plusieurs points méritent d'être gardés à l'esprit :

segments.src: - Currency moves depend on many factors, not just rate differences. These include growth, trade flows, and investor appetite for risk.
segments.tr: - Les mouvements de change dépendent de nombreux facteurs, pas seulement des différences de taux. Il s'agit notamment de la croissance, des flux commerciaux et de l'appétit des investisseurs pour le risque.

segments.src: - The dollar often strengthens during periods of global uncertainty, which can offset the effect of narrower rate gaps.
segments.tr: - Le dollar se renforce souvent en période d'incertitude mondiale, ce qui peut compenser l'effet du rétrécissement des écarts de taux.

segments.src: - Markets usually price in expected moves before they happen. A rate rise that was widely expected may have little effect on the day.

segments.src: ## What happened
segments.tr: ## O que aconteceu

segments.src: - **United Kingdom:** The Bank of England lifted its policy rate to 4%. That is the first rate rise in over three years, and it ends a period in which markets had mostly expected cuts.
segments.tr: - **Reino Unido:** O Banco da Inglaterra elevou sua taxa de juros básica para 4%. Esse é o primeiro aumento de juros em mais de três anos, e encerra um período em que os mercados esperavam majoritariamente cortes.

segments.src: - **Australia:** The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates five times this year. That makes it one of the most active tightening central banks among advanced economies.
segments.tr: - **Austrália:** O Banco da Reserva da Austrália aumentou as taxas cinco vezes este ano. Isso o torna um dos bancos centrais de aperto mais ativos entre as economias avançadas.

segments.src: Each says it is trying to bring inflation back toward its goal.
segments.tr: Cada um diz que está tentando trazer a inflação de volta à sua meta.

segments.src: ## Why inflation is picking up again
segments.tr: ## Por que a inflação está voltando a subir

segments.src: Inflation rarely rises for one reason.
segments.tr: A inflação raramente sobe por um único motivo.

segments.src: Several forces are commonly cited in cases like these:
segments.tr: Várias forças são comumente citadas em casos como estes:

segments.src: 1. **Sticky services prices.** Wages, rents and insurance costs tend to move slowly. When they keep rising, headline inflation is slow to cool.
segments.tr: 1. **Preços de serviços rígidos.** Salários, aluguéis e custos de seguro tendem a se mover lentamente. Quando continuam subindo, a inflação cheia demora a esfriar.

segments.src: 2. **Energy and food costs.** Swings in energy and food prices can lift inflation quickly. They also affect what households expect inflation to be.
segments.tr: 2. **Custos de energia e alimentos.** Oscilações nos preços de energia e alimentos podem elevar a inflação rapidamente. Eles também afetam o que as famílias esperam que seja a inflação.

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** Where employers still struggle to hire, wage growth can stay high enough to keep price pressure up.
segments.tr: 3. **Mercados de trabalho apertados.** Onde os empregadores ainda lutam para contratar, o crescimento salarial pode permanecer alto o suficiente para manter a pressão sobre os preços.

segments.src: 4. **Inflation expectations.** If households and firms expect higher prices, they may set wages and prices accordingly. Central banks want to stop that cycle early.
segments.tr: 4. **Expectativas de inflação.** Se famílias e empresas esperam preços mais altos, elas podem definir salários e preços de acordo. Os bancos centrais querem interromper esse ciclo cedo.

segments.src: 5. **Currency moves.** A weaker local currency makes imports more expensive, which can feed into consumer prices.
segments.tr: 5. **Movimentos cambiais.** Uma moeda local mais fraca torna as importações mais caras, o que pode alimentar os preços ao consumidor.

segments.src: Which of these matters most differs by country.
segments.tr: Qual destes importa mais difere por país.

segments.src: That is one reason central banks do not all move at the same time.
segments.tr: Essa é uma das razões pelas quais os bancos centrais não se movem todos ao mesmo tempo.

segments.tr: Os bancos centrais respondem a dados diferentes.

segments.src: A bank that sees inflation staying above target, or rising again, may judge that waiting is riskier than acting.

segments.src: ## What it could mean for the dollar
segments.tr: ## O que isso pode significar para o dólar

segments.src: Exchange rates reflect the gap between interest rates in different places.
segments.tr: As taxas de câmbio refletem a lacuna entre as taxas de juros em diferentes lugares.

segments.src: When other central banks raise rates while the Federal Reserve holds steady, the difference narrows.
segments.tr: Quando outros bancos centrais aumentam as taxas enquanto o Federal Reserve se mantém estável, a diferença diminui.

segments.src: That can make other currencies somewhat more attractive relative to the dollar.
segments.tr: Isso pode tornar outras moedas um pouco mais atraentes em relação ao dólar.

segments.src: Several points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: Vários pontos valem a pena ter em mente:

segments.src: - Currency moves depend on many factors, not just rate differences. These include growth, trade flows, and investor appetite for risk.
segments.tr: - Os movimentos cambiais dependem de muitos fatores, não apenas das diferenças de taxas. Estes incluem crescimento, fluxos comerciais e apetite dos investidores por risco.

segments.src: - The dollar often strengthens during periods of global uncertainty, which can offset the effect of narrower rate gaps.
segments.tr: - O dólar frequentemente se fortalece durante períodos de incerteza global, o que pode compensar o efeito de lacunas de taxas mais estreitas.

segments.src: - Markets usually price in expected moves before they happen. A rate rise that was widely expected may have little effect on the day.
segments.tr: - Os mercados geralmente precificam os movimentos esperados antes que eles aconteçam. Um aumento de taxa que era amplamente esperado pode ter pouco efeito no dia.

segments.tr: 過去2年間の大部分において、金融政策の世界的潮流は利下げでした。

segments.src: Now a few central banks are moving the other way.

segments.src: The Reserve Bank of Australia has tightened five times this year.

segments.src: This article explains what is behind those decisions and what they could mean for U.S.

segments.src: ## What happened
segments.tr: ## 何が起きたのか

segments.src: - **United Kingdom:** The Bank of England lifted its policy rate to 4%. That is the first rate rise in over three years, and it ends a period in which markets had mostly expected cuts.
segments.tr: - **イギリス：** イングランド銀行は政策金利を4%に引き上げました。これは3年ぶりの利上げであり、市場が主に利下げを予想していた期間に終止符を打つものです。

segments.src: - **Australia:** The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates five times this year. That makes it one of the most active tightening central banks among advanced economies.
segments.tr: - **オーストラリア：** オーストラリア準備銀行は今年に入って5回利上げを行っています。これにより、同国は先進国の中で最も積極的に引き締めを行っている中央銀行の一つとなっています。

segments.src: Both banks have said their decisions follow the data.
segments.tr: 両行とも、その決定はデータに従ったものであると述べています。

segments.src: Neither has described them as a break from their inflation targets.
segments.tr: どちらも、インフレ目標からの逸脱であるとは説明していません。

segments.src: Each says it is trying to bring inflation back toward its goal.
segments.tr: それぞれ、インフレを目標値に戻そうとしているのだと主張しています。

segments.src: ## Why inflation is picking up again
segments.tr: ## なぜインフレが再び加速しているのか

segments.src: Inflation rarely rises for one reason.
segments.tr: インフレが単一の理由で上昇することはまれです。

segments.src: Several forces are commonly cited in cases like these:
segments.tr: このような場合、いくつかの要因が一般的に挙げられます：

segments.src: 1. **Sticky services prices.** Wages, rents and insurance costs tend to move slowly. When they keep rising, headline inflation is slow to cool.
segments.tr: 1. **根強いサービス価格。** 賃金、家賃、保険料は動きが遅い傾向があります。これらが上昇し続けると、総合インフレ率はなかなか低下しません。

segments.src: 2. **Energy and food costs.** Swings in energy and food prices can lift inflation quickly. They also affect what households expect inflation to be.
segments.tr: 2. **エネルギー・食料品コスト。** エネルギーや食料品価格の変動は、インフレを急速に押し上げる可能性があります。また、家計のインフレ期待にも影響を与えます。

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** Where employers still struggle to hire, wage growth can stay high enough to keep price pressure up.
segments.tr: 3. **ひっ迫した労働市場。** 雇用主が依然として採用に苦労している地域では、賃金上昇率が価格圧力を維持するのに十分な高水準にとどまる可能性があります。

segments.src: 4. **Inflation expectations.** If households and firms expect higher prices, they may set wages and prices accordingly. Central banks want to stop that cycle early.
segments.tr: 4. **インフレ期待。** 家計や企業が物価上昇を予想する場合、それに応じて賃金や価格を設定する可能性があります。中央銀行はその循環を早期に止めたいと考えています。

segments.src: 5. **Currency moves.** A weaker local currency makes imports more expensive, which can feed into consumer prices.
segments.tr: 5. **為替の動き。** 自国通貨安は輸入品をより高価にし、それが消費者物価に波及する可能性があります。

segments.src: Which of these matters most differs by country.
segments.tr: これらのうちどれが最も重要かは、国によって異なります。

segments.src: That is one reason central banks do not all move at the same time.
segments.tr: それが、中央銀行が一斉に同じタイミングで動かない理由の一つです。

segments.src: ## Why some banks hike while others wait

segments.src: A bank that sees inflation staying above target, or rising again, may judge that waiting is riskier than acting.
segments.tr: インフレ率が目標を上回り続けている、あるいは再び上昇していると見る中央銀行は、行動しないことの方がリスクが大きいと判断するかもしれません。

segments.src: A bank that sees slowing growth and cooling prices may choose to hold.
segments.tr: 成長の鈍化や物価の冷却を見ている中央銀行は、据え置きを選択するかもしれません。

segments.src: Rate increases also carry costs.

segments.src: Higher borrowing costs weigh on mortgage holders, small businesses and government budgets.
segments.tr: 借入コストの上昇は、住宅ローン利用者、中小企業、政府の予算に負担をかけます。

segments.src: Policymakers weigh those costs against the risk of letting inflation settle at a higher level.
segments.tr: 政策当局者は、そうしたコストと、インフレを高水準で定着させてしまうリスクとを比較衡量しています。

segments.src: ## What it could mean for the dollar

segments.src: Exchange rates reflect the gap between interest rates in different places.
segments.tr: 為替レートは、さまざまな地域の金利差を反映しています。

segments.src: When other central banks raise rates while the Federal Reserve holds steady, the difference narrows.
segments.tr: 他の中央銀行が利上げを行う一方で連邦準備制度（FRB）が据え置きを維持すると、その差は縮小します。

segments.src: That can make other currencies somewhat more attractive relative to the dollar.
segments.tr: これにより、ドルに対して他の通貨がやや魅力的になることがあります。

segments.src: Several points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: いくつかの点を心に留めておく価値があります：

segments.src: - Currency moves depend on many factors, not just rate differences. These include growth, trade flows, and investor appetite for risk.

segments.src: ## Why inflation is picking up again

segments.src: 2. **Energy and food costs.** Swings in energy and food prices can lift inflation quickly. They also affect what households expect inflation to be.

segments.src: ## What it could mean for the dollar

vi.title: Tăng lãi suất trong khi các bên khác chờ đợi: Tại sao Ngân hàng Trung ương Anh và Australia lại tiếp tục tăng lãi suất

segments.src: For much of the past two years, the global story in monetary policy was about cutting.
segments.tr: Trong phần lớn thời gian hai năm qua, câu chuyện toàn cầu về chính sách tiền tệ là việc cắt giảm lãi suất.

segments.src: Now a few central banks are moving the other way.
segments.tr: Giờ đây, một số ngân hàng trung ương đang đi theo hướng ngược lại.

segments.src: The Bank of England has raised its benchmark rate to 4%, its first increase in more than three years.
segments.tr: Ngân hàng Trung ương Anh đã nâng lãi suất cơ bản lên 4%, mức tăng đầu tiên trong hơn ba năm.

segments.src: The Reserve Bank of Australia has tightened five times this year.
segments.tr: Ngân hàng Dự trữ Australia đã thắt chặt năm lần trong năm nay.

segments.src: This article explains what is behind those decisions and what they could mean for U.S.
segments.tr: Bài viết này giải thích những gì đằngหลัง các quyết định đó và ý nghĩa của chúng đối với độc giả

segments.tr: Chi tiết về các quyết định chính sách có thể thay đổi nhanh chóng, vì vậy hãy kiểm tra các tuyên bố chính thức của ngân hàng trung ương để biết các số liệu mới nhất.*

segments.src: ## What happened
segments.tr: ## Chuyện gì đã xảy ra

segments.src: - **United Kingdom:** The Bank of England lifted its policy rate to 4%. That is the first rate rise in over three years, and it ends a period in which markets had mostly expected cuts.
segments.tr: - **Vương quốc Anh:** Ngân hàng Trung ương Anh đã nâng lãi suất chính sách lên 4%. Đây là đợt tăng lãi suất đầu tiên trong hơn ba năm qua và chấm dứt giai đoạn mà thị trường phần lớn kỳ vọng sẽ cắt giảm lãi suất.

segments.src: - **Australia:** The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates five times this year. That makes it one of the most active tightening central banks among advanced economies.
segments.tr: - **Australia:** Ngân hàng Dự trữ Australia đã tăng lãi suất năm lần trong năm nay. Điều này khiến đây trở thành một trong những ngân hàng trung ương thắt chặt hoạt động tích cực nhất trong số các nền kinh tế phát triển.

segments.src: Both banks have said their decisions follow the data.
segments.tr: Cả hai ngân hàng đều cho biết các quyết định của họ tuân theo dữ liệu.

segments.src: Neither has described them as a break from their inflation targets.
segments.tr: Không bên nào mô tả chúng là sự phá vỡ các mục tiêu lạm phát của họ.

segments.src: Each says it is trying to bring inflation back toward its goal.
segments.tr: Mỗi bên đều cho biết họ đang cố gắng đưa lạm phát trở lại mục tiêu của mình.

segments.src: ## Why inflation is picking up again
segments.tr: ## Tại sao lạm phát lại tăng trở lại

segments.src: Inflation rarely rises for one reason.
segments.tr: Lạm phát hiếm khi tăng vì một lý do duy nhất.

segments.src: Several forces are commonly cited in cases like these:
segments.tr: Một số lực lượng thường được nhắc đến trong các trường hợp như thế này:

segments.src: 1. **Sticky services prices.** Wages, rents and insurance costs tend to move slowly. When they keep rising, headline inflation is slow to cool.
segments.tr: 1. **Giá dịch vụ cứng nhắc.** Tiền lương, tiền thuê nhà và chi phí bảo hiểm có xu hướng di chuyển chậm. Khi chúng tiếp tục tăng, lạm phát cơ bản sẽ giảm chậm.

segments.src: 2. **Energy and food costs.** Swings in energy and food prices can lift inflation quickly. They also affect what households expect inflation to be.
segments.tr: 2. **Chi phí năng lượng và thực phẩm.** Sự biến động của giá năng lượng và thực phẩm có thể làm tăng lạm phát nhanh chóng. Chúng cũng ảnh hưởng đến kỳ vọng lạm phát của các hộ gia đình.

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** Where employers still struggle to hire, wage growth can stay high enough to keep price pressure up.
segments.tr: 3. **Thị trường lao động thắt chặt.** Nơi mà người sử dụng lao động vẫn gặp khó khăn trong việc tuyển dụng, tăng trưởng tiền lương có thể duy trì ở mức đủ cao để giữ áp lực giá cả.

segments.src: 4. **Inflation expectations.** If households and firms expect higher prices, they may set wages and prices accordingly. Central banks want to stop that cycle early.
segments.tr: 4. **Kỳ vọng lạm phát.** Nếu các hộ gia đình và doanh nghiệp kỳ vọng giá cả cao hơn, họ có thể thiết lập tiền lương và giá cả cho phù hợp. Các ngân hàng trung ương muốn ngăn chặn chu kỳ đó sớm.

segments.src: 5. **Currency moves.** A weaker local currency makes imports more expensive, which can feed into consumer prices.
segments.tr: 5. **Biến động tiền tệ.** Đồng nội tệ yếu hơn làm cho hàng nhập khẩu đắt hơn, điều này có thể tác động vào giá tiêu dùng.

segments.src: Which of these matters most differs by country.
segments.tr: Yếu tố nào quan trọng nhất sẽ khác nhau tùy theo quốc gia.

segments.src: That is one reason central banks do not all move at the same time.
segments.tr: Đó là lý do tại sao các ngân hàng trung ương không phải lúc nào cũng hành động cùng một lúc.

segments.src: ## What happened
segments.tr: ## क्या हुआ

segments.src: - **United Kingdom:** The Bank of England lifted its policy rate to 4%. That is the first rate rise in over three years, and it ends a period in which markets had mostly expected cuts.
segments.tr: - **यूनाइटेड किंगडम:** बैंक ऑफ इंग्लैंड ने अपनी नीतिगत दर को बढ़ाकर 4% कर दिया है। यह तीन साल से अधिक समय में पहली दर वृद्धि है, और यह उस अवधि को समाप्त करती है जिसमें बाजारों को ज्यादातर कटौती की उम्मीद थी।

segments.src: - **Australia:** The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates five times this year. That makes it one of the most active tightening central banks among advanced economies.
segments.tr: - **ऑस्ट्रेलिया:** रिजर्व बैंक ऑफ ऑस्ट्रेलिया ने इस साल पांच बार दरें बढ़ਾਈ हैं। यह इसे उन्नत अर्थव्यवस्थाओं में सबसे सक्रिय रूप से सख्ती बरतने वाले केंद्रीय बैंकों में से ایک बनाता है।

segments.src: Both banks have said their decisions follow the data.
segments.tr: दोनों बैंकों ने कहा है कि उनके निर्णय आंकड़ों का अनुसरण करते हैं।

segments.src: Neither has described them as a break from their inflation targets.
segments.tr: किसी ने भी इन्हें अपने मुद्रास्फीति लक्ष्यों से ब्रेक के रूप में वर्णित नहीं किया है।

segments.src: Each says it is trying to bring inflation back toward its goal.
segments.tr: प्रत्येक का कहना है कि वह मुद्रास्फीति को उसके लक्ष्य की ओर वापस लाने का प्रयास कर रहा है।

segments.src: ## Why inflation is picking up again
segments.tr: ## मुद्रास्फीति फिर से क्यों बढ़ रही है

segments.src: Inflation rarely rises for one reason.
segments.tr: मुद्रास्फीति शायद ही कभी एक कारण से बढ़ती है।

segments.src: Several forces are commonly cited in cases like these:
segments.tr: इस तरह के मामलों में आम तौर पर कई ताकतों का हवाला दिया जाता है:

segments.src: 1. **Sticky services prices.** Wages, rents and insurance costs tend to move slowly. When they keep rising, headline inflation is slow to cool.
segments.tr: 1. **चिपचिपी सेवाएं कीमतें।** मजदूरी, किराया और बीमा लागत धीरे-धीरे बढ़ने की प्रवृत्ति रखते हैं। जब वे बढ़ती रहती हैं, तो हेडलाइन मुद्रास्फीति ठंडी होने में धीमी होती है।

segments.src: 2. **Energy and food costs.** Swings in energy and food prices can lift inflation quickly. They also affect what households expect inflation to be.
segments.tr: 2. **ऊर्जा और भोजन की लागत।** ऊर्जा और खाद्य कीमतों में उतार-चढ़ाव मुद्रास्फीति को तेजी से बढ़ा सकते हैं। वे इस बात को भी प्रभावित करते हैं कि परिवार मुद्रास्फीति क्या होने की उम्मीद करते हैं।

segments.src: 3. **Tight labor markets.** Where employers still struggle to hire, wage growth can stay high enough to keep price pressure up.
segments.tr: 3. **तंग श्रम बाजार।** जहां नियोक्ता अभी भी काम पर रखने के लिए संघर्ष करते हैं, वहां मजदूरी वृद्धि इतनी अधिक रह सकती है कि मूल्य दबाव बना रहे।

segments.src: 4. **Inflation expectations.** If households and firms expect higher prices, they may set wages and prices accordingly. Central banks want to stop that cycle early.
segments.tr: 4. **मुद्रास्फीति की उम्मीदें।** यदि परिवार और फर्म उच्च कीमतों की उम्मीद करते हैं, तो वे तदनुसार मजदूरी और कीमतें तय कर सकते हैं। केंद्रीय बैंक उस चक्र को जल्दी रोकना चाहते हैं।

segments.src: 5. **Currency moves.** A weaker local currency makes imports more expensive, which can feed into consumer prices.
segments.tr: 5. **मुद्रा चालें।** एक कमजोर स्थानीय मुद्रा आयात को अधिक महंगा बनाती है, जो उपभोक्ता कीमतों में फीड हो सकती है।

segments.src: Which of these matters most differs by country.
segments.tr: इनमें से कौन सा सबसे अधिक मायने रखता है, यह देश के अनुसार भिन्न होता है।

segments.src: That is one reason central banks do not all move at the same time.
segments.tr: यह एक कारण है कि केंद्रीय बैंक सभी एक ही समय में नहीं चलते हैं।

segments.src: ## Why some banks hike while others wait
segments.tr: ## कुछ बैंक दरें क्यों बढ़ाते हैं जबकि अन्य इंतजार करते हैं

segments.src: Central banks answer to different data.
segments.tr: केंद्रीय बैंक विभिन्न आंकड़ों का जवाब देते हैं।

segments.src: A bank that sees inflation staying above target, or rising again, may judge that waiting is riskier than acting.
segments.tr: एक बैंक जो देखता है कि मुद्रास्फीति लक्ष्य से ऊपर बनी हुई है, या फिर से बढ़ रही है, वह यह निर्णय ले सकता है कि इंतजार करना कार्रवाई करने से अधिक जोखिम भरा है।

segments.src: A bank that sees slowing growth and cooling prices may choose to hold.
segments.tr: एक बैंक जो धीमी वृद्धि और ठंडी कीमतों को देखता है, वह रुकना चुन सकता है।

segments.src: Rate increases also carry costs.
segments.tr: दर में वृद्धि के साथ लागत भी आती है।

segments.src: Higher borrowing costs weigh on mortgage holders, small businesses and government budgets.
segments.tr: उच्च उधार लागत बंधक धारकों, छोटे व्यवसायों और सरकारी बजट पर भार डालती है।

segments.src: Policymakers weigh those costs against the risk of letting inflation settle at a higher level.
segments.tr: नीति निर्माता मुद्रास्फीति को उच्च स्तर पर बसने देने के जोखिम के खिलाफ उन लागतों का वजन करते हैं।

segments.src: ## What it could mean for the dollar
segments.tr: ## डॉलर के लिए इसका क्या अर्थ हो सकता है

segments.src: Exchange rates reflect the gap between interest rates in different places.
segments.tr: विनिमय दरें विभिन्न स्थानों पर ब्याज दरों के बीच की खाई को दर्शाती हैं।

segments.src: When other central banks raise rates while the Federal Reserve holds steady, the difference narrows.
segments.tr: जब अन्य केंद्रीय बैंक दरें बढ़ाते हैं जबकि फेडरल रिजर्व स्थिर रहता है, तो अंतर संकीर्ण हो जाता है।

segments.src: That can make other currencies somewhat more attractive relative to the dollar.
segments.tr: यह डॉलर के सापेक्ष अन्य मुद्राओं को कुछ अधिक आकर्षक बना सकता है।

segments.src: Several points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: ध्यान में रखने योग्य कई बिंदु हैं:

segments.src: - Currency moves depend on many factors, not just rate differences. These include growth, trade flows, and investor appetite for risk.
segments.tr: - मुद्रा चालें कई कारकों पर निर्भर करती हैं, न कि केवल दर अंतर पर। इनमें विकास, व्यापार प्रवाह और जोखिम के लिए निवेशक की भूख शामिल हैं।

segments.src: - The dollar often strengthens during periods of global uncertainty, which can offset the effect of narrower rate gaps.
segments.tr: - डॉलर अक्सर वैश्विक अनिश्चितता की अवधि के दौरान मजबूत होता है, जो संकीर्ण दर अंतराल के प्रभाव को ऑफसेट कर सकता है।

segments.src: - Markets usually price in expected moves before they happen. A rate rise that was widely expected may have little effect on the day.
segments.tr: - बाजार आमतौर पर होने से पहले अपेक्षित चालों की कीमत तय करते हैं। एक दर वृद्धि जिसकी व्यापक रूप से उम्मीद की जाती थी, उसका दिन पर बहुत कम प्रभाव हो सकता है।

segments.tr: ## आयात कीमतें और दैनिक लागत
